description.text: **Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Safety-Guard-8B-v3** is a multilingual content safety model that moderates human-LLM interaction content and classifies user prompts and LLM responses as safe or unsafe. If the content is unsafe, the model additionally returns a response with a list of categories that the content violates. It supports 9 languages: English, Spanish, Mandarin, German, French, Hindi, Japanese, Arabic, and Thai. The base large language model (LLM) is the multilingual Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model from Meta. NVIDIA’s optimized release is LoRa-tuned on approved datasets and better conforms to NVIDIA’s content safety risk taxonomy and other safety risks in human-LLM interactions. The model is trained using the Nemotron-Safety-Guard-Dataset-v3 dataset which is synthetically curated using the CultureGuard pipeline. The model shows strong zero-shot generalization supporting over 20 languages (en, ar, de, es, fr, hi, ja, th, zh, it, ko, nl, cs, da, fi, iw, pt-BR, pl, ru, sv).

output_type.quote: classifies user prompts and LLM responses as safe or unsafe

serving.notes: The card says context length up to 8K. config.json max_position_embeddings and the tokenizer model_max_length are 131072. The usage example sets max_new_tokens=100. The safety-policy text is passed as the user message, not as a system role. The repository contains four full safetensors shards (8,030,261,248 BF16 parameters) and a separate lora_adapter (r=8, alpha=32, dropout 0.05, targets q_proj and v_proj). The card says the adapter weights are provided separately. The paper states a per-GPU batch size of 4 on 8 A100s. The paper names the checkpoint Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Safety-Guard-8B-v3 and does not print the Hugging Face repository id. The paper's dataset count is 386,661 samples in 9 languages; the current Hub dataset has 514,617 rows in 12 languages.

evaluation_reported.text: Card table of scores: Nemotron-Safety-Guard-Dataset-v3 85.32, PolyGuardPrompts 76.07, RTP-LX 91.49, MultiJail 95.36, XSafety 66.97, Aya Red-teaming 96.79. The paper reports harmful-F1 and says the model improves 31.06% relative to Llama-Nemotron-Safety-Guard-V2 on multilingual scores.
